name: Chapli Kabab
description: Pashtun-style flat beef kababs with crushed coriander, cumin, herbs and tomato, shallow-fried until browned outside and fully cooked inside.
ingredients: 750 g beef mince with some fat
1 medium tomato, finely chopped and excess juice removed
1 small onion, finely chopped and squeezed of excess moisture
1 tsp red chili flakes or to taste
method: Combine the mince, onion, green chilies, coriander, crushed coriander and cumin, chili flakes, maize flour, egg and salt. Mix until evenly combined.
Fold in the chopped tomato just before shaping so the mixture does not become excessively wet.
With damp hands, shape the mixture into broad, thin patties. Chill for 10–15 minutes if the mixture feels too soft.
Heat a shallow layer of oil over medium heat. Fry the kababs in batches without crowding the pan.
Cook until deeply browned on both sides and the centre is fully cooked; ground beef should reach 71°C/160°F.
Drain briefly and serve hot with chutney, naan and salad.
tips: Remove excess moisture from onion and tomato to help the kababs hold together.
Make the patties relatively thin so the centre cooks before the exterior burns.
storage: Refrigerate cooked kababs promptly in a covered container for up to 2 days and reheat until piping hot.
